title: The Geography of Sustainable Convergence
subtitle: Population Growth, Development Disparities and Resilience Across Emerging Economies
description: An H Heuristics spatial and demographic synthesis within the Polycrisis Resilience Series— concept developed by Hunter Hughes—examining where population…
contribution: Introduces a spatial and demographic dimension to Sustainable Convergence within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series—concept developed by Hunter Hughes—analyzing the intersections of demographic, economic, environmental, and resilience dynamics across five emerging macro-regions.
abstract: The Geography of Sustainable Convergence is a flagship publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).

keyFindings.title: Global population growth through 2100 will concentrate overwhelmingly in Sub-Saharan Africa (1.24B → 3.34B) and South Asia (1.98B → 2.05B), making spatial infrastructure and secondary-city resilience the decisive determinant of global convergence.

Without geographically targeted investment, Spatially Uneven Drift depresses the Emerging-Economy Sustainable Convergence Index from 41.5 (2025) to 33.0 by 2100; Geographically Balanced Convergence lifts it to 90.5 by 2100.
Region-tailored portfolios deliver 9.8x–12.1x 25-year social benefit-cost ratios—led by Sub-Saharan Africa Clean Grids & STEM (12.1x) and South Asia Urban Cooling & Clean Air (11.4x).

Examining the intersections of demographic, economic, environmental, and resilience dimensions compresses regional Polycrisis Vulnerability across Sub-Saharan Africa (83.5 → 14.0) and South Asia (74.5 → 12.0) while lifting regional GDP/capita to 74–89.5% of the OECD frontier.
